title: In More Than 8% of the Sensor Videos Declassified by PURSUE, the UAP Might be Birds

content:
3 min read

Just now

--

The first paper from the UAP Science Advisory Council, posted recently here, analyzed a swarm of six infrared dots moving in a coordinated fashion, with intelligent maneuvering capabilities that supersede drones. This raised the intriguing question: might this be evidence for alien technology?

The video showing the six dots, labeled DOW-UAP-PR135, was declassified as evidence for an Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) by the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE) on September 18, 2026.

Our analysis paper, led by Dr. Jacob Haqq-Misra, found that the brightness of these dots varies periodically about 7–8 times per second, consistently with infrared videos of birds flapping their wings taken by the Galileo Project observatories, as described recently here. The infrared brightness reflects the heat radiated from the body of a bird which depends on the area and orientation of the bird’s wings, triggering periodic variations as the bird flaps its wings. The flapping rate of birds increases with increasing altitude as the surrounding air gets more rarefied.

This result changed an officially declared Unidentified Anomalous Phenomenon (UAP) to a potential Identified Phenomenon (IP) in terms of flying animals. Indeed, some animals have collective behaviors more sophisticated than our best robots or drones. The great benefit of periodic brightness variations as an identification method is that it does not depend on the unknown distance to UAP.

Encouraged by the match between DOW-UAP-PR135 and the birds in the Galileo Project’s data, Jacob went on to apply the same analysis method to all the sensor video released so far in the six tranches of PURSUE. This brought the count up to 10 PURSUE videos containing a total of 25 bird candidates. This count amounts to about 8% of the sensor videos released so far, including PR41, PR44, PR077, PR079, PR085, PR088, PR097, PR099, and PR141. The new results include one video, PR097, with a likely flock of four birds followed by four other birds later in the clip. Another video PR141 shows a split screen with infrared and optical channels both displayed for the object; both wavelengths show a similar variability frequency for the object. Other videos probably show birds but are too faint and grainy to capture a reliable beat frequency.

This additional data analysis was added as “Supplementary Information” in the paper posted here.

***

Which fraction of the remaining 88% of the declassified sensor videos involve unidentified birds or human-made drones? The infrared characteristics of slow objects in the triangulated Galileo Project data reported here might be a useful training data set for AI algorithms attempting to answer this question.

As I emphasized recently here and here, science is done by analysis of data collected by instruments and not by storytelling on social media. The scientific research on UAP demonstrates the value of science in resolving their nature, be it flying animals, Chinese spy drones or alien technology.

Avi Loeb is chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council to the White House, Pentagon, FBI and intelligence agencies, director of the Galileo Project, founding director of Harvard University’s — Black Hole Initiative, former director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics, and the former chair of the astronomy department at Harvard University (2011–2020).
